source.title: Fast Generalization after Interpolation via Critically Damped Momentum Optimization
source.authors: Luca Muscarnera; Silas Ruhrberg Estévez; Yuanzhang Xiao; M. van der Schaar

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including supplementary information, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests post-interpolation generalization and norm minimization using a new biphasic optimizer, with synthetic algorithmic benchmarks and other settings; it does not reproduce the original grokking method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports endpoint scores on several synthetic benchmarks, but those scores alone do not establish delayed generalization. It also reports test-accuracy trajectories for Binary Addition and Modular Addition, language-model validation-loss trajectories, norm/test-loss results, and a post-interpolation representation analysis. Other benchmark endpoint scores are not included because they do not measure the timing or mechanisms named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is an optimizer paper. It takes grokking's two-phase view (fit, then norm minimization) as motivation for GROKtimizer and reports mainly that method's performance against Adam, AdamW, Muon and SGD, as endpoint scores and trajectories. It never measures delayed generalization arising under ordinary training. It does not report training-accuracy saturation or delay length, and does not vary training-set size against delay. The language-model and Gaussian post-interpolation gains come from the study's own optimizer switch, not from grokking arising on its own.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim, theoretically, a quadratic speedup over gradient descent from critically damped momentum under a local quadratic model, and say it is optimal among first-order methods. They link post-interpolation dynamics to flat minima via the dimension of the Hessian null space. They state that data-constrained settings limit the scope.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes GROKtimizer: unregularized fitting to interpolation followed by critically damped, weight-decayed momentum. It uses grokking as motivation but does not reproduce the original training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes across datasets and optimizer choices. The language-model experiments use an unregularized SGD-based interpolation phase; the text says applying weight decay too early can hinder fitting. An elevated post-interpolation learning rate makes Adam unstable in the Binary Addition and Modular Addition comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST and CIFAR-10, interpolating solutions obtained at different initialization scales show test cross-entropy rising roughly as a power law of parameter norm, with exponent about 3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Among interpolating neural-network solutions, test loss scales polynomially with parameter norm.

fits_no_version.finding: NTK-based representations become more class-separated during post-interpolation norm minimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-interpolation norm-minimization training progressively reorganizes NTK representations after the training labels are fit.

record.problems: The plotted grokking-benchmark accuracy trajectories are not numerically reported in the text, and the paper does not state training-accuracy saturation alongside them. The language-model evidence is described as a small validation-loss reduction and uses 14M- and 38M-parameter models. Several reported results are plotted without numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: Endpoint results for the other synthetic and real-world benchmarks in Tables 1 and 2 are not included: they do not report the temporal behavior or mechanisms named by the tested versions. No other rows were left out for the versions tested.

untested.parts: Delayed test-accuracy jump after training saturation, and delay versus training-set size. Neither is measured.
Gradual circuit formation and progress measures are not examined.
There is no test of switching delay on or off through initialization or weight norm. Initialization scale is varied only for the static loss–norm plot.
There is no measure of naturally occurring delayed generalization in realistic LLM training.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking are not tested.
Untested. The paper notes that Adam is unstable at a high learning rate, but only as an ablation.

record.verdict_notes: Classified as T4. It is a method paper using grokking's two-phase framing, and every trajectory result concerns the study's own optimizer. The record's V1, V4 and V5 links and its labels are removed. The WeightWatcher alpha trend (Fig. 10) is also a diagnostic of the study's own method.

versions.untested_parts: The paper plots test-accuracy trajectories for Binary Addition and Modular Addition, but does not report training-accuracy saturation alongside them in the text. It does not test whether shrinking the training set increases the delay.
The NTK representation analysis does not identify a generalizing circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that a continuous progress measure anticipates a test-accuracy jump.
No test of switching grokking-like delays on or off through initialization scale, weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
The language-model experiments use 14M- and 38M-parameter models; the paper does not test large-scale LLM training.
The study tests norm minimization and generalization associations, but not whether a more efficient circuit is selected, a critical dataset size exists, or ungrokking occurs below it.
No comparison of whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
The paper does not test whether grokking delays are artifacts of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point limits in the softmax.
